evidence.actual: Root isolated full-app QA605385: original YouTube live mouse fullscreen enters; Escape fails with main focus and again after native-video focus. Original mouse exit button succeeds and restores the floating layout. This proves a keyboard-path defect, not its exact cause.
evidence.code: Both original_page.js and original_vod_page.js accept Escape from a noneditable body in the exact player document while their fullscreen flag is true. There is no movie_player closest gate. The native receiver independently requires the physical key still down in GetAsyncKeyState during asynchronous WebMessageReceived. No existing gate-reason log can distinguish released key, focus mismatch or an absent message.
evidence.inference: A short keydown can be released before asynchronous bridge delivery, but this is only a candidate until the actual classified gate result is observed. Do not remove a guard or call the keyboard bug fixed from this candidate.

proposal.classification: Return a fixed enum for the existing guard's first failure: invalid_input, window_unavailable, key_released, focus_mismatch, pointer_outside, accepted. Preserve the same check ordering, APIs, foreground/pane/focus/physical-button conditions and final permission result; trusted_input remains an equivalent bool wrapper for other callers.
proposal.logging: Only after the existing canonical source, label, message and current document epoch checks, log a recognized fullscreen mouse/f/escape action and the fixed gate enum. Limit to32 events per native WebView bridge lifetime using an atomic saturating budget. No arbitrary keys, strings, URL/query, document content, identifiers, account values or HWND values. No input interception, polling, synthetic input or focus repair.
proposal.scope: YouTube LIVE and VOD bridge routes only. The classification helper is shared but SOOP/CHZZK admission behavior and logging remain unchanged. No new trusted origin, privilege, account or authentication behavior.
proposal.conflicts: Root cannot safely hold a key with the current UI tool. Diagnostics collect evidence instead of weakening physical intent checks to make automated short key presses pass. Existing native mouse success is preserved.
